DO NOT BUY FISH HERE. We initially bought a blood parrot and electric blue acara and they both got ich within 2 days and the acara died within 6. We were able to save the blood parrot and decided to go back and try our hand at another acara but this time we set up a quarantine tank to try and save it because we notice that the other ones already had ich. This time it only survived 3 days while being very carefully treated for ich in an extremely stable cycled tank with the correct water perimeters at 78 degrees. It never even showed signs of ich but was very ill either from ammonia burns or a bacterial infection. Either way save yourself the trouble and go to a reputable local fish store like old town Aquarium or aquatic world.

The staff is super friendly, the prices are competitive with other stores, if not better, on certain items, and the additional amenities of the self-wash & dry or the nail and ear services are done make this the best spot in the neighborhood for most of your everyday pet needs.

⛔️BEWARE: SHADY REWARDS PROGRAM!!!!!⛔️

I’ve been shopping exclusively here for years for my two cats and dog (including grooming), but as of today I’m done, and I’m so disappointed. I’ve been a rewards member  since 2022 and recently used a $5 reward to buy some canned cat food. My cats are picky so I bought 10 cans thinking I could return them if they don’t like them. When I brought 8 cans back today, I learned rewards coupons can’t be exchanged, so the $5 was just forfeit—even though I was exchanging it for $30 in dry food, $4 in wet food, cat nip, and a nail trim for my dog. They said it was policy. I found that hard to believe (because it’s absurd) so I emailed corporate and they linked their policy and sure enough, rewards coupons are forfeited. Gift cards too! So if you buy something with a gift card that needs to be exchanged, you’ll simply lose that money. I can understand not returning something purchased with rewards for cash (this makes sense) but to not provide store credit on earned rewards is just sinister. And to think they’re targeting their most loyal customers with this bad policy!

It’s not about the $5 to me (it’s $5…) but the principle of it. There are other stores to buy pet food that have fairer policies. And honestly, when there are sinister policies like this, it’s likely you find other issues within organizations: usually labor issues, employee mistreatment, precarious working environments, etc. And considering this business sells live animals, I have to assume there are likely ethical issues there too.

I’ll be taking my business elsewhere.
